A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BMC research, with matching methodology and substantial retained experiments. All 19 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original QA, mathematical-reasoning, and instruction-following experiments, together with component ablations, reward analyses, and appendix experiments comparing response-editing LLMs.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds comparator evaluations, modification-proportion experiments, semantic-similarity analysis, runtime measurements, and Qwen2.5-14B results.

M1.justification: The targeted-editing Bridging Phase and confidence-weighted Modeling Phase remain unchanged, including the loss, stop-gradient operation, clipping threshold, and token-difference identification. New baselines and backbone evaluations do not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets and ten evaluation benchmarks across QA, mathematics, and instruction following. Qwen2.5-14B and partial data modification introduce model and experimental configurations, not new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 remove KTO and TDPO and introduce DPO (CW), which generates losing responses by continuing winning-response prefixes, and DPO (EW), which uses external token weighting. This substantially revises the comparison set across all three task families, adding targeted controls while dropping established optimization alternatives.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen2.5-14B-Base configuration, a six-level modification-proportion sweep from 0% to 100%, embedding-based similarity measurement, and runtime comparisons. The established benchmark metrics, dataset splits, training budgets, and retained-model hyperparameters remain unchanged; these are additional evaluation settings.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 tests how much preference data requires modification; Section 5.1 adds semantic-similarity evidence concerning reverse-editing failures; Appendix B adds synthesis-cost and training-overhead analyses. These substantially extend sensitivity and efficiency analysis. The earlier editing-LLM ablation, delta sweep, KL analysis, and case study are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes SimPO-BMC's reported instruction-following score from 19.7 to 21.9, reversing its ranking against unchanged SimPO at 21.3, without explaining the revision. New Qwen2.5-14B results report BMC/DPO scores of 45.1/36.3 on AlpacaEval 2 and 40.9/33.6 on Arena-Hard. Comparator rows, modification-proportion findings, similarity scores, and cost/runtime results are added, while KTO/TDPO rows disappear. Retained main BMC scores and relocated reward-analysis results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The DPO and BMC formulations in Equations 1–6 and the Appendix C gradient analysis are retained. Expanded discussion of informative gradients supplies conceptual explanation rather than a new mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two-phase contribution, performance claims across QA/math/instruction following, and versatility to DPO variants. Removing illustrative improvement numbers from the introduction does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes superficial prefix correlations from informative preference differences and explains reverse-editing difficulties through LLMs' training toward high-quality outputs. It adds interpretations concerning partial modification, practical cost, and larger-model gains. Section 5.4 removes the SimPO failure qualification and the stated reasons for excluding KTO/TDPO adaptations; the existing KL interpretation is merely relocated.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly reports API pricing assumptions, input/output token lengths, synthesis budgets, measured training times, and deployment guidance. Section 5.1 identifies the all-mpnet-base-v2 similarity model. Conversely, the retained reward analysis loses its explicit 2,000-sample validation-set disclosure, and removed baselines lose their tuning details. Core prompts, hyperparameters, and repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lee et al. (2024) for external weighting and Qwen Team (2024), while removing the KTO and TDPO references. Related-work exposition is shortened, but the central positioning around correlated preference data and dynamic token weighting remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized revisions condense the introduction, related work, and Section 5.2 while expanding the bridging explanation and revising Sections 5.1 and 5.4. Appendices are reorganized around cost and larger-model experiments. Main-section ordering and most exposition remain stable; publication headers and author contact information are updated.

P2.justification: The evidence displays are substantially reorganized: v3 adds modification-proportion Figure 3 and cost/runtime/model-comparison Tables 9–11, moves v2 Table 9 into main-text Table 4, and relocates v2 Figure 4 to appendix Figure 9. The sequence-reward table becomes prose, comparison-table rows change, and several captions are shortened. Retained graphics largely preserve their original content.

improvement.justification: New Figure 3 and Appendix B address previously unquantified modification requirements and computational costs, while targeted CW/EW controls and the larger-model evaluation strengthen empirical support. These provide a limited overall improvement to an already extensively evaluated method. Benefits are tempered by removing KTO/TDPO comparisons, losing the validation-set-size disclosure, and leaving the SimPO-BMC score revision unexplained.
